v.why: Skip is already a decent substitute, so the conv gain is smaller than when replacing none or pooling.
1x1 conv is a close substitute for 3x3 so the upgrade gain is small.
A parent already holding a 3x3 conv has less headroom, so the gain shrinks.
Strong parents with conv into the output saturate and gain less from another conv.
A conv already feeding node 2 provides a substitute, so the added conv helps less.
A strong conv path to the output already exists so the skip gain shrinks.
A skip already present on the direct path makes another skip largely redundant.
Adding a skip when one already exists gives little additional benefit.
Skip is generally better than pooling, so replacing pool with skip gains versus replacing stronger ops.
Removing a weak pooling edge costs little compared with removing a conv or skip.
